reflections.title: "The Lord Sees the Heart"

reflect.text: We often form quick opinions about people based on how they look, their charm, or their social standing. Even the prophet Samuel made this mistake. When he saw Jesse's oldest son, he assumed that such a tall, handsome man had to be God's choice for king. But God reminded Samuel that human beings judge by outward traits, while the Lord sees the heart. Our culture often values status and wealth, but God values inner devotion and humility.

While his older brothers stood before the prophet, David was out in the pasture faithfully caring for the family sheep. God bypassed the outwardly impressive brothers to choose an inexperienced shepherd whom others might overlook. Having a heart that pleases God does not mean being perfect or avoiding hardship. David faced deep struggles and failures, yet he consistently turned back to God in repentance. God looks for quiet faithfulness and a heart wholly dependent on him.

questions: In what ways might you be judging yourself or others by outward appearances rather than the heart?
How can you practice quiet faithfulness in the everyday tasks God has given you right now?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us when we judge people by how they look instead of seeing them as you do. Search our hearts and make us humble and faithful in the small things. Help us to keep turning back to you in complete trust, no matter what difficulties we face. Amen.

reflections.title: Anointed with the Holy Spirit

reflect.text: In a single day, David went from tending sheep in the fields to being anointed as king. Yet as writer F. B. Meyer observed, "an even greater blessing came into his life that day," because the Holy Spirit rushed upon him in power. From that moment forward, God gave David the spiritual strength and presence he needed to carry out his calling. The Spirit of God was not just with him in secret, but now rested upon him to lead and serve.

We may not be chosen to wear an earthly crown, but God offers this same divine power to his people today. Even Jesus did not begin his public ministry until the Holy Spirit rested upon him at his baptism. It is foolish to try to do God's work in our own human strength. God invites us to come to him, set ourselves apart for his glory, and ask for the Holy Spirit's help. We can ask him daily for renewed power so that we may live faithfully as his witnesses.

questions: Are you trying to live the Christian life or serve others in your own strength rather than relying on the Holy Spirit?
How might asking God for the Holy Spirit's power change how you face today's tasks?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank you for sending your Holy Spirit to live in us and guide us. Forgive us for trying to do your work in our own human strength. Fill us afresh today with power from on high so that our lives bring glory to you. Amen.
